name: Antimanual Builder – Truly AI Powered Visual Page Builder
author: Spider Themes

sections.description:
Antimanual Builder is a truly AI-powered, drag-and-drop visual page builder that brings a Replit/Lovable-style website building experience to WordPress. Describe the page you want in plain language and get a complete, editable layout back — then keep refining it by chat or by hand.

It’s a full-screen design canvas for native WordPress pages: no Gutenberg, no separate “builder” post type, and no lock-in. Every page you create is a regular WordPress page post, so your content stays portable and works with your theme, permalinks, and other plugins.

Build pages with AI. Generate whole layouts from a prompt, ask for changes conversationally, and migrate existing pages with AI assistance — all inside the editor. You have two ways to power the AI:

  • WordPress AI Connectors (WordPress 7.0+) — point Builder at the AI provider built into WordPress core for one-shot page generation, with nothing extra to install.
  • The free Antimanual companion plugin — connect your own provider and API key to unlock the live editor chat, knowledge base, and conversational refinement. Works with OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, and OpenCode Zen.

Or build entirely by hand. Every page is fully editable with drag-and-drop layout tools, inline canvas editing, reusable components, header/footer templates, and a responsive live preview. Manual editing and page migration work standalone — no API key and no external service required. Add AI when you want it; Builder keeps working fully without it.

Live Demo | Documentation | Support Forum | Upgrade to Premium

Video Overview

Build With AI

  • Generate from a prompt — Describe the page you want and get a complete, fully editable layout back inside the editor.
  • Refine conversationally — Ask for changes in chat and watch the page update, section by section.
  • AI-assisted migration — Redesign or restructure an existing WordPress page with AI help.
  • Two AI sources — Use the built-in WordPress AI Connectors (WordPress 7.0+) for one-shot generation, or the free Antimanual companion plugin for the full chat and knowledge-base experience.
  • Bring your own provider — Through Antimanual, works with OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, and OpenCode Zen.
  • Your keys, your control — Builder reads the provider, model, and API key you configure in the Antimanual companion plugin; keys are never managed or exposed by Builder itself.

Build Visually

  • Full-screen visual editor — A distraction-free canvas for native WordPress pages, with no Gutenberg required.
  • Drag-and-drop & inline editing — Arrange sections and edit text directly on the canvas, entirely without AI.
  • Structured block system — Layout, content, and advanced blocks power both manual editing and generated pages.
  • Responsive preview — Check layouts in Desktop, Tablet, Large Mobile, and Small Mobile widths before you publish.
  • Code editor tabs — Inspect and tweak HTML, CSS, and JavaScript alongside the visual canvas.
  • Undo/Redo — Full editing history with keyboard shortcuts.
  • Version history — Every save keeps the previous version, restorable from a History panel.
  • Crash recovery — Unsaved changes are backed up in your browser and offered back if the tab closes before you save.

Reuse & Scale

  • Component library — Save any section as a reusable component and insert it on any page, with live previews, search, and category filters.
  • Push updates to components — Update a saved component and roll the change out to the pages that use it, while leaving hand-edited copies alone.
  • Header & footer templates — Build and assign reusable templates through a visual picker with live thumbnails.
  • Design Defaults — Set the tone, design system, typography, spacing, corners, and brand colors applied to new pages.

Bring In Existing Content

  • Page migration — Migrate an existing WordPress page into Builder as a faithful, fully editable copy — replace the original or keep a copy.
  • CDN libraries — Attach external CSS and JavaScript libraries from a CDN, controlling load position and async/defer behavior.
  • HTML & ZIP import (Pro) — Import a single HTML file with its assets, or analyze and create whole pages from a ZIP project, with chunked upload and a progress bar for large sites.
  • Dynamic content binding (Pro) — Bind a section to your real site content so it updates automatically, or turn a section into a live navigation menu.

How It Works

  1. Open AM Builder from the WordPress admin menu and create a new page (or migrate an existing one).
  2. Build your layout with drag-and-drop sections, saved components, and inline editing — or, with the Antimanual plugin active, describe it in chat.
  3. Preview across device sizes, then publish. The page is a standard WordPress page, live on your site with your theme’s header and footer.

Generated and imported assets are stored in wp-content/uploads/antimanual-builder/.

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services.

OpenAI API

Powers AI chatbot, knowledge base embeddings, and all content generation features when OpenAI is the selected provider. Your WordPress post content (for KB indexing), visitor chat messages, and admin-configured prompts are sent to OpenAI via your own API key. Data is transmitted only when you trigger an AI action or a visitor interacts with the chatbot/search.

  • OpenAI — Terms — Privacy

Google Gemini API

One of Antimanual’s supported AI providers. The same categories of data described for OpenAI above are sent to Google Gemini via your own API key, only when Gemini is the active provider.

  • Google AI (Gemini) — Terms — Privacy

Additional AI Providers

Depending on the provider you configure, Antimanual may also send your WordPress post content (for knowledge base indexing where supported), visitor chat messages, and admin-configured prompts to Anthropic Claude, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, or OpenCode Zen only when you trigger an AI action or a visitor interacts with the chatbot or AI search.

  • Anthropic
  • xAI
  • DeepSeek
  • OpenCode Zen

Spider Themes Notice Service

The plugin periodically fetches an admin notice from Spider Themes servers to display important announcements to site administrators. Only a standard HTTP GET request is made — no personal data, site content, or visitor information is ever transmitted.

  • Spider Themes — Terms — Privacy

Placehold.co (Placeholder Images)

AI-generated pages may include placeholder images served by Placehold.co.

  • What it does: Provides temporary placeholder images (solid-color rectangles with optional text) that appear in AI-generated page layouts until the user replaces them with real images.
  • What is sent: The visitor’s browser requests images from placehold.co when viewing a page that still contains placeholder image URLs. Only the requested image dimensions and optional label text are included in the URL — no user data or personal information is transmitted by the plugin itself.
  • When: Only when a generated page contains unreplaced placeholder image URLs and a visitor (or the admin previewing the page) loads that page.

Fonts

The plugin does not load fonts from Google Fonts, Bunny Fonts, Adobe Typekit, Font Awesome, or any other third-party font CDN.

  • The editor UI uses the operating system’s native font stack (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif).
  • AI-generated pages are instructed to use the same system font stack. The AI is explicitly told not to add @import rules or <link> tags pointing at remote font hosts.
  • As a defensive measure, any @import or <link> that references a known font CDN is stripped from saved page CSS/HTML on the server before it is persisted, even if the AI model ignores the prompt.
  • If a user imports their own HTML (e.g. via the ZIP importer), the original markup — including any font references the user authored themselves — is preserved as-is, because that content is owned by the user, not generated by the plugin.

Security / Arbitrary Code

The builder does not support arbitrary PHP, JavaScript, or CSS insertion. There is no code-editor UI that accepts raw CSS, JS, or PHP and no REST endpoint that persists author-supplied stylesheets or scripts.

  • No arbitrary CSS: Page CSS is generated programmatically from block style values and from a structured styleMap of selector/property pairs collected through the visual editor’s form controls. The plugin does not store free-form CSS authored by users.
  • No arbitrary JavaScript: Only hard-coded interactive scripts that ship with the plugin (tabs, accordion, counter, etc.) are emitted, and they are gated on the corresponding block being present on the page. There is no input surface for user-supplied JavaScript.
  • No arbitrary PHP: There is no PHP code input in the UI and no REST endpoint that accepts or executes PHP supplied by users.
  • REST sanitization: The customCss / customJs request parameters are stripped from all save endpoints (/wp-json/ambld/v1/pages, /components, /templates). Inline <style>, <script>, and on*= event-handler attributes are removed from renderedHtml and from imported documents before storage.
  • Render-time defence-in-depth: Frontend output is passed through wp_kses() with a strict allowlist that excludes <script> and <style>, so any data that may have been persisted by older versions of the plugin cannot be served.
  • Legacy cleanup: On upgrade, the plugin removes any _ambld_custom_css / _ambld_custom_js post meta and any per-post src/post-{ID}.css / .js files left behind by earlier releases.

Source Code

The human-readable source code for all compiled JavaScript and CSS assets is included in the src/ directory of this plugin.

  • Source files: src/editor/, src/admin/, src/page-editor/
  • Build tool: wp-scripts (WordPress webpack configuration)
  • Build command: npm install && npm run build
  • Compiled output: build/editor.js, build/admin.js, build/page-editor.js and their corresponding CSS files

The webpack.config.js at the plugin root defines three entry points. All dependencies are managed via package.json.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the antimanual-builder folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Antimanual Builder.
  3. Open AM Builder from the WordPress admin menu and start building pages — manual editing, HTML import, components, and templates work out of the box.
  4. (Optional) To enable AI generation/refinement, also install and activate the free Antimanual plugin and configure your AI provider and API key there.
sections.faq:
How do I build my first page?

Open AM Builder from the WordPress admin menu, create a new page, and start adding sections with the drag-and-drop tools. You can edit text inline on the canvas, insert saved components, preview across device sizes, and publish — all without an AI key or any external service.

Do I need the Antimanual plugin?

No. Antimanual Builder works fully standalone for manual editing, direct migration, HTML/ZIP import, components, and templates. The separate Antimanual plugin is needed only for the optional AI features — it connects your AI provider and sets up the knowledge base used for generation, refinement, and AI-based migration.

Do I need an AI API key?

Only for the optional AI features such as generation, refinement, and AI-based migration. Manual editing, direct migration, components, templates, and HTML import work without an AI key.

Which AI provider should I use?

When the Antimanual plugin is installed, Builder uses whichever provider you have configured in it. Supported providers include OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, and OpenCode Zen.

Where do I configure AI providers?

In the optional Antimanual plugin. When it is installed and active, Builder reads the active provider, model, and API key status from there. Without it, the AI features are simply unavailable but the rest of Builder works.

Can I use this alongside other page builders?

Yes, but Builder edits native WordPress pages rather than a separate builder page post type. Use migration intentionally on the pages you want Builder to manage.

What happens to my pages if I deactivate the plugin?

Your pages remain in WordPress because they are standard page posts. The Builder editing layer is what’s removed, but the published content stays part of your site. Uninstalling cleans up what the plugin created while keeping your content (pages, templates, designs, chat history) unless you opt in to full removal.

Will my pages match my theme?

Yes. Builder pages render as native WordPress pages, so they appear inside your active theme with its header and footer. You can also assign your own Builder header/footer templates per page.

Does it load any external fonts or trackers?

No. The editor and generated pages use your operating system’s native font stack, and the plugin does not load fonts from any third-party CDN. AI providers are contacted only when you explicitly trigger an AI action, and only if you’ve installed the optional Antimanual plugin. See the “External services” section for full details.

Where are generated assets stored?

Generated/imported assets are stored in wp-content/uploads/antimanual-builder/.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0 (11 September 2026)

  • Added: Templates tab in the editor — 36 ready-made starter templates for pages, blocks, and headers/footers. Preview one at desktop, tablet, or mobile width, then create a draft from it in one click.
  • Added: Use this template can hand the new page straight to AI Chat, which rewrites the demo copy into your own content using what it remembers about your site and your knowledge base.
  • Added: Six standalone showcase designs — Alba, Vector, Studio Index, Fluid Studio, Nova, and Yanxi Onsen — imported whole, keeping their original fonts, motion, and layout.
  • Added: Insert a starter component into an empty section on the canvas, with search and category filters.
  • Added: A catalogue of 42 named motion effects (curtain reveals, clip wipes, marquees, magnetic cursors, rolling counters, and more), each with a full implementation spec the AI follows exactly.
  • Added: Long messages you send in chat now collapse to two lines behind a fade, with an arrow to expand them.
  • Added: Antimanual Cloud AI with free monthly credits — no API key setup. Chat shows the remaining balance and stops when credits run out.
  • Added: Background Build can update existing pages — pick specific pages or all of them — instead of only creating new ones (Pro).
  • Added: Site Header & Footer page template — wrap Builder content in your theme’s header and footer, without the theme’s inner page layout.
  • Added: Page migration copies this site’s stylesheets, scripts, and fonts so migrated pages keep working after the source plugin or theme updates.
  • Added: An Assets screen to review and update the copied CSS, JS, and fonts that migrated pages depend on.
  • Added: Page migration keeps your SEO plugin titles, descriptions, and related data.
  • Added: Set a page’s parent from the editor and from Quick Edit.
  • Improved: The AI treats motion as part of building a page, not a finishing touch — it picks two to four named effects and applies them consistently instead of inventing something different for every section.
  • Improved: Plans now name the motion effects the page will use, so you approve the animation along with the layout — in chat plan mode and in background site builds.
  • Improved: Starter templates can be free or Pro; Pro ones preview in full and link to an upgrade.
  • Improved: Quick Edit opens in a modal instead of inside the list row.
  • Improved: Page migration captures published pages as visitors see them, without logged-in admin scripts such as Elementor Notes.
  • Fixed: Migrated pages on Theme Default now load their imported stylesheets on the live site, not only in the editor canvas.
  • Fixed: Theme Default pages keep the WordPress admin bar spacing when you are logged in.
  • Fixed: Clicks, menus, and chat widgets on migrated pages keep working after save.
  • Fixed: Migrated pages no longer show stuck loaders or leftover top spacing from the original page.
  • Fixed: Contact forms on builder pages now collect real submissions instead of being blocked by the page’s own success script.
  • Fixed: Stop and New chat now cancel the in-flight AI turn instead of leaving it running in the background.

1.1.0 (22 August 2026)

  • Added: Form capture and default notification email on the Settings page — turn collection off site-wide, and choose where new entries are emailed when a form has not set its own recipients.
  • Added: Set a page’s categories, tags, and featured image from the editor’s page settings.
  • Added: The AI can read and update a page’s title, slug, status, excerpt, categories, tags, and featured image — including when creating a new page.
  • Added: Quick-start prompts when you open a blank header, footer, or component.
  • Added: Queue follow-up prompts in chat while the AI is still working.
  • Added: Pick a WordPress AI Connectors provider or model (or Auto) in Settings and in chat.
  • Added: Drag a saved block from the insert menu onto a specific spot on the canvas.
  • Added: Duplicate a component from the Components admin list.
  • Added: HTML import asks you to upload missing stylesheets, scripts, images, and fonts before creating the page (Pro).
  • Improved: The editor Settings sidebar is denser, with smaller fields, type, and spacing.
  • Improved: Page and element settings now share one Settings sidebar with Page and Element tabs.
  • Improved: Switch between Antimanual and WordPress AI Connectors from the chat panel, not only Settings.
  • Improved: Hierarchy drag-and-drop lets you nest or promote items by moving left and right.
  • Improved: Header and footer template thumbnails and untitled placeholders are clearer and more accurate.
  • Improved: Draft and private pages no longer offer a save when nothing has changed.
  • Improved: The save button shows progress while a save is in flight.
  • Improved: Saved blocks keep their styles, colors, and scripts when you reuse them on another page.
  • Improved: Save a block from the sidebar, not only the canvas right-click menu.
  • Improved: Switching between AM Builder admin screens is instant, without reloading the whole page.
  • Improved: Admin lists can show 500 rows or every row at once.
  • Fixed: With WordPress AI Connectors selected, the AI agent can run its tools again.
  • Fixed: Saves no longer strip boolean or empty attributes.
  • Fixed: Saves no longer bake temporary preview states (like open menus) into the page HTML.
  • Fixed: Selection outlines now show on clipped images.
  • Fixed: The Hierarchy panel follows the element you click or drag on the canvas.
  • Fixed: Replacing or editing an image or link on the canvas now targets the one you clicked, not a previously selected one.
  • Fixed: Published pages keep HTML5 and SVG tags and attributes instead of stripping them on the live site.
  • Fixed: Imported HTML pages now match the import preview in the editor and on the live site (Pro).
  • Fixed: Draft pages in the admin list show a real date instead of an invalid one.

1.0.0 (14 August 2026)

  • Added: The AI chat agent can browse a web page you point it to and read its text, colors, fonts, and outside libraries, so it can work from real reference material.
  • Added: When asked to review a whole site, the AI agent now follows the site’s links and sitemap to check other pages instead of stopping at the homepage.
  • Added: Agent Memory — the AI can save durable facts like brand rules or preferences that carry over into future conversations, with a new “Agent Memory” tab in Settings to review or delete them.
  • Added: The AI can now ask to look back at an image you attached earlier in the conversation, instead of only remembering that you sent it.
  • Added: The AI can take a screenshot of the editor canvas — and scroll it first — to see how the page looks while it edits.
  • Added: A chat setting to turn those AI canvas screenshots on or off.
  • Added: An optional “Show cost estimates” chat setting that shows an estimated dollar cost for each AI turn and tool step, using your model’s published rates.
  • Added: An Example Prompts picker in chat, with searchable examples for live search, forms, and other advanced builds.
  • Added: Form Submissions — forms on your builder pages now collect what visitors send, into a new Submissions screen with unread, read, spam, and trash views.
  • Added: Each new entry is emailed as it arrives, to the addresses and subject line that form chooses in the editor, with reply-to set to the visitor.
  • Added: Export your form entries to a CSV spreadsheet, honouring whichever filter you are viewing.
  • Added: Per-form settings in the editor — the form’s name, the thank-you message visitors see after sending, and an opt-out for forms that shouldn’t be collected.
  • Added: An unread count on the AM Builder menu, so new entries are never missed.
  • Added: Search boxes on builder pages now really search your site, with no setup needed.
  • Added: A ready-made Search block in the editor’s insert menu, with sidebar settings for its label, placeholder, and button style.
  • Added: A page’s own scripts can fetch your published posts, categories, products, and site search results through a built-in helper, so custom filters, live search, and load-more work without inventing URLs.
  • Added: The AI can look up what your site really contains — its post types, categories, tags, menus, and custom fields — so it stops guessing names that don’t exist (Pro).
  • Added: The AI can connect a section to your live content on its own, and checks the connection against your content before saving (Pro).
  • Added: Ask the AI to confirm that every connected section on a page is returning real content, and which fields will show up blank (Pro).
  • Added: Show WooCommerce products in a section, with their real price, rating, stock, and best-seller order (Pro).
  • Added: Let visitors filter a connected list with a dropdown or a search box, with no scripting needed (Pro).
  • Added: “Show more” buttons can reveal the next batch of items, using the button your page already has (Pro).
  • Added: Connect a parent–child section — cards for parent pages with a nested list of their children inside each card (Pro).
  • Added: The builder’s page list now shows each page’s address.
  • Added: Background Build — describe a multi-page site in chat, then run the build as a background job and follow progress from the admin notifications bell (Pro).
  • Added: Drag sections and elements into place directly on the page canvas, not only from the hierarchy panel.
  • Added: Convert several WordPress pages to AM Builder at once from the Pages list, and follow progress from the admin notifications bell.
  • Improved: The AI now picks its design references from a browsable library instead of a search index, so design guidance works on every provider, needs no re-indexing, and costs nothing extra per request.
  • Improved: The AI can also draw on your own saved headers, footers, and components as design references, so “make it like my other page” works.
  • Improved: You are now told when the AI stopped mid-answer because it ran out of room, instead of the reply quietly ending half finished.
  • Improved: The AI now stops repeating a failed action instead of retrying it dozens of times, and tells you plainly when it got stuck.
  • Improved: When an AI provider fails — including rate limits — the editor now names the provider and the reason, with clearer guidance on what to do next.
  • Improved: Each AI tool step in the chat now shows how many tokens it used, and cached tokens are counted separately when the provider reports them.
  • Improved: Switch AI provider from the chat panel, not only the model.
  • Improved: The Dynamic Content dialogs and the sidebar binding panel have been redesigned to match the rest of the editor.
  • Improved: The editor now explains when an element can’t be made dynamic, or has moved since you selected it, instead of failing silently.
  • Improved: Connected sections in the editor now show your site’s real content instead of stand-in samples.
  • Improved: Navigation menus connected to WordPress now show their dropdown sub-items, instead of only the top level (Pro).
  • Improved: The editor now previews your site’s real menu items instead of sample links.
  • Improved: The sidebar now warns you when an imported page renders as an exact copy of the original document, where no theme or plugin code runs.
  • Improved: Migrating a page waits longer before giving up on slow or heavy sites.
  • Fixed: AI-generated sections no longer run edge to edge — their content now has proper width and side spacing, both on the published page and in the editor preview.
  • Fixed: Choosing the Full-Width page template now actually makes the page full width, instead of only marking it.
  • Fixed: A shortcode block no longer prints its editor placeholder and the raw shortcode text onto the published page next to the real output.
  • Fixed: Scripts a plugin emits through a shortcode in a header or footer template now run, instead of showing up as visible text on the page.
  • Fixed: Content other plugins add to a page — related posts, share buttons, and the like — now appears on builder pages instead of being discarded.
  • Fixed: Builder pages now output one page title instead of two, leaving your SEO plugin’s title as the only one.
  • Fixed: A page that lists other pages can no longer loop endlessly and exhaust the site’s memory.
  • Fixed: Clicking a row in the editor’s element list now simply selects it, instead of folding it away — only the arrow folds it.
  • Fixed: The importer no longer opens to a blank screen.
  • Fixed: Imported pages are now created at the addresses the import screen listed.
  • Fixed: A connected section no longer shows the same items twice (Pro).
  • Fixed: Live content is no longer wiped out when a post’s own text contains double curly braces, such as an article about templating (Pro).
  • Fixed: Newer OpenAI models that still rejected tool use after the automatic retry now continue when reasoning is forced off.
  • Fixed: Page titles and labels no longer show garbled text like & instead of &.
  • Fixed: Your theme’s form fields and styles no longer override the design on builder pages.
  • Fixed: AI-built pages keep their styles on the published site when they use the standalone layout, instead of looking unstyled.
  • Fixed: Refreshing the page while the AI is waiting for your answer no longer breaks Submit on the question card.
  • Security: Saving a page as an author who doesn’t hold the script permission now clears that permission, so newly added scripts can never run under an earlier author’s.

See changelog for all versions.

  • What is sent: The visitor’s browser requests images from placehold.co when viewing a page that still contains placeholder image URLs. Only the requested image dimensions and optional label text are included in the URL — no user data or personal information is transmitted by the plugin itself.
  • When: Only when a generated page contains unreplaced placeholder image URLs and a visitor (or the admin previewing the page) loads that page.

Fonts

The plugin does not load fonts from Google Fonts, Bunny Fonts, Adobe Typekit, Font Awesome, or any other third-party font CDN.

  • The editor UI uses the operating system’s native font stack (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif).
  • AI-generated pages are instructed to use the same system font stack. The AI is explicitly told not to add @import rules or <link> tags pointing at remote font hosts.
  • As a defensive measure, any @import or <link> that references a known font CDN is stripped from saved page CSS/HTML on the server before it is persisted, even if the AI model ignores the prompt.
  • If a user imports their own HTML (e.g. via the ZIP importer), the original markup — including any font references the user authored themselves — is preserved as-is, because that content is owned by the user, not generated by the plugin.

Security / Arbitrary Code

The builder does not support arbitrary PHP, JavaScript, or CSS insertion. There is no code-editor UI that accepts raw CSS, JS, or PHP and no REST endpoint that persists author-supplied stylesheets or scripts.

  • No arbitrary CSS: Page CSS is generated programmatically from block style values and from a structured styleMap of selector/property pairs collected through the visual editor’s form controls. The plugin does not store free-form CSS authored by users.
  • No arbitrary JavaScript: Only hard-coded interactive scripts that ship with the plugin (tabs, accordion, counter, etc.) are emitted, and they are gated on the corresponding block being present on the page. There is no input surface for user-supplied JavaScript.
  • No arbitrary PHP: There is no PHP code input in the UI and no REST endpoint that accepts or executes PHP supplied by users.
  • REST sanitization: The customCss / customJs request parameters are stripped from all save endpoints (/wp-json/ambld/v1/pages, /components, /templates). Inline <style>, <script>, and on*= event-handler attributes are removed from renderedHtml and from imported documents before storage.
  • Render-time defence-in-depth: Frontend output is passed through wp_kses() with a strict allowlist that excludes <script> and <style>, so any data that may have been persisted by older versions of the plugin cannot be served.
  • Legacy cleanup: On upgrade, the plugin removes any _ambld_custom_css / _ambld_custom_js post meta and any per-post src/post-{ID}.css / .js files left behind by earlier releases.

Source Code

The human-readable source code for all compiled JavaScript and CSS assets is included in the src/ directory of this plugin.

  • Source files: src/editor/, src/admin/, src/page-editor/
  • Build tool: wp-scripts (WordPress webpack configuration)
  • Build command: npm install && npm run build
  • Compiled output: build/editor.js, build/admin.js, build/page-editor.js and their corresponding CSS files

The webpack.config.js at the plugin root defines three entry points. All dependencies are managed via package.json.
